title: Sciences of observation
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-3, 10-11, and 17-18: opening assumptions, observer definition, memory, and conclusion.
version: Published Philosophies article, October 10, 2018.
caveats: Cross-disciplinary review and proposed interface ontology; panpsychist and zero-net-information suggestions are interpretive, not established by the survey.

title: Mind is an abstraction
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-3, Fields commentary only, especially paragraphs 3-16. Adjacent commentaries on the same printed pages were excluded.
version: Published commentary, Constructivist Foundations 13(3), 350-352, 2018.
caveats: Philosophical criticism and tentative ontology; no empirical or mathematical consciousness result.

title: First-person science is third person and vice versa
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-2, entire Fields commentary, paragraphs 1-16; adjoining author response excluded.
version: Published commentary, Constructivist Foundations 13(2), 240-241, 2018.
caveats: Conceptual argument about scientific practice; no convergence theorem or mathematical identification of social and quantum reference frames.

title: Conscious agent networks: Formal analysis and application to cognition
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-2, 6-7, 12-13, 20-21, 29-30, and 45-46: definition, kernel assumptions, composition, memory, and conclusion.
version: Author-linked manuscript dated August 29, 2017; published in Cognitive Systems Research 47 (2018), 186-213.
caveats: Formal architecture and finite constructions; homogeneous kernels, specified copying operations, and conscious-realism interpretation. General formation and relative clocks remain open.

title: Object permanence
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-9: definition, short/long intervals, developmental questions, self, time, evolutionary discussion, and conclusion.
version: Author-linked encyclopedia-entry manuscript; homepage identifies 2017 online entry 2373 with DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-16999-6_2373-1.
caveats: Review with a speculative interface-theory interpretation; no new experiment and no established mechanism linking temporal experience to permanence.

title: Eigenforms, interfaces and holographic encoding: Toward an evolutionary account of objects and spacetime
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-3, 5-6, and 8-10: primary article introduction, interface comparison, holography discussion, coding proposal, and conclusion.
version: Published 2017 package, Constructivist Foundations 12(3), pp. 265-291 including commentaries and response. Primary article occupies pp. 265-274; this note does not summarize the separate commentaries.
caveats: Spacetime-as-code and its dimensionality argument are proposals; abstract boundary information capacity is not a derived gravitational area law.
verified_metadata_corrections: The homepage citation spans the complete article/commentary package; BibTeX identifies the primary article pages.

title: Building the observer into the system: Toward a realistic description of human interaction with the world
pages_read: PDF pp. 1, 5, 10-12, 19, and 24: setting, black-box definition, Moore/no-boundary arguments, identification, and conclusion.
version: Published Systems 4(4), 32, October 28, 2016.
caveats: Finite-observation and unconstrained black-box setting; absence of externally guaranteed separability is part of the no-boundary argument. Quantum correspondences are not independently adjudicated here.

title: Unitary quantum theory as a formal framework for a theory of consciousness
pages_read: PDF pp. 1 and 11-13: abstract, proposed theory of reportable experience, and conclusion.
version: Author-linked 16-page chapter manuscript; homepage identifies the 2016 New Age Books volume, pp. 127-146.
caveats: Interpretive consciousness proposal; no validated identification of entanglement with experience and no derived classical-to-quantum equivalence.

title: Visual re-identification of individual objects: A core problem for organisms and AI
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-2, 8, and 12-13: problem statement, causal re-identification, epistemic feelings, and conclusion.
version: Author-linked 23-page manuscript; publication citation is Cognitive Processing 17 (2016), 1-13, DOI 10.1007/s10339-015-0736-3.
caveats: Review and proposed robotics research program; heuristic identity inference and subjective confidence are not exact sufficiency or precision theorems.

title: Science generates limit paradoxes
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-2, 5, 13, 17, and 22: motivation, apophenia example, Ladder Schema, Inclosure mapping, and conclusion.
version: Author-linked manuscript dated March 18, 2015; published Axiomathes 25 (2015), 409-432.
caveats: Philosophical diagnosis depends on universalizing its examples and on the epistemic premises of the schema; it is not a general inconsistency theorem for science.

title: Reverse engineering the world: A commentary on Hoffman, Singh and Prakash, "The interface theory of perception"
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-9: complete commentary body, including system identification, virtual machines, evolutionary hypothesis, and quantum coda.
version: Author-linked 10-page commentary manuscript; published in Psychonomic Bulletin & Review 22 (2015), 1526-1529.
caveats: Commentary and comparative hypothesis; no new experiment, exact coarse-graining, or derivation of quantum mechanics. Black-box underdetermination assumes no restrictive model class.

title: Motion, identity and the bias toward agency
pages_read: PDF pp. 1, 4-5, 9-10, 12, and 15-17: proposal, developmental context, causal-history mechanism, test designs, and conclusion.
version: Author-linked 26-page manuscript; published as Frontiers in Human Neuroscience 8 (2014), article 597.
caveats: Review-based mechanistic hypothesis with proposed tests; causal-history implementation, developmental extensions, and evolutionary explanation are not experimentally established here.

title: A physics-based metaphysics is a metaphysics-based metaphysics
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-3, 12-14, and 19-22: framing, subsystem argument, monism discussion, rejoinder, and conclusion.
version: Author-linked 27-page manuscript; published in Acta Analytica 29 (2014), 131-148.
caveats: Philosophical critique. The claim that entanglement removes subsystem Hilbert spaces conflates lack of separate pure states with lack of a specified tensor-product structure.

title: This boundary-less world
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-3, 10-13, and 17-19: framing, decomposition argument, observation limits, causal histories, and philosophical conclusion.
version: Author-hosted 20-page chapter PDF; author catalog identifies chapter 13 of Brain, Mind, Cosmos (2014), edited by Deepak Chopra.
caveats: Popular philosophical exposition; boundary-free ontology, quantum analogies, time interpretation, and panpsychism exceed what decomposition invariance and finite records alone establish.

title: How humans solve the frame problem
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-3, 5-6, and 10-11: task definition, object-token and memory mechanisms, proposed solution, and conditional conclusion.
version: Author manuscript marked in press, August 2012; journal publication is 2013, volume 25, 441-456.
caveats: The frame-problem equivalence is conditional on the fictive-causal-history model and scoped to human cognition; no unrestricted computational solution or new experiment.

title: On recognizing an object with a partition
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-2 and 4-10: recognition definition, completeness/exclusivity argument, black-box identification, consistent histories, quantum discussion, and conclusion.
version: Author manuscript dated July 11, 2013; published in Logique et Analyse 56(224), 391-403.
caveats: Critique of fully objective reference under unrestricted hidden alternatives; practical partitions remain allowed. Quantum ontological claims are not established by the finite-observation argument.

title: A whole box of Pandoras: Systems, boundaries and free will in quantum theory
pages_read: PDF pp. 1, 4-5, 7, and 10-14: proposal, observer/system distinction, virtual-machine formulation, probability discussion, semantic freedom, and conclusion.
version: Author manuscript dated October 7, 2012; published in the 2013 special issue on Paradox and Mind, volume 25, 291-302.
caveats: Proposed quantum interpretation; Born rule is inherited from the universal theory, physical origin of semantic maps remains open, and semantic freedom is not a proof of controllable causal freedom.

title: The principle of persistence, Leibniz's law, and the computational task of object re-identification
pages_read: PDF pp. 1, 4, 8-9, and 13-16: implementation question, developmental argument, long-gap re-identification, proposed experiments, and conclusion.
version: Author-linked manuscript marked Human Development in press; published in 2013, volume 56, 147-166.
caveats: Critical review and heuristic architecture; no new experiment. Informational underdetermination should not be confused with a formal computational-complexity theorem.

title: The very same thing: Extending the object token concept to incorporate causal constraints on individual identity
pages_read: PDF pp. 1-2, 6-7, and 9-11: motivation, BIC-FCH construction and Figure 2, neural hypothesis, clinical proposals, and conclusion.
version: Published Advances in Cognitive Psychology article, volume 8(3), 234-247 (2012); PDF includes journal pagination and DOI.
caveats: Review-based BIC-FCH hypothesis; direct controlled testing remains required, category updating is incompletely specified, and clinical extensions are unvalidated proposals.

title: Trajectory recognition as the basis for object individuation: A functional model of object file instantiation and object token encoding
pages_read: PDF pp. 1, 4, and 8-10: object-file definition, STR hypotheses, trajectory abstraction, predictions, and conclusion.
version: Published Frontiers in Psychology Hypothesis and Theory article, March 25, 2011, volume 2, article 49; official journal PDF replaces the unusable author-hosted download.
caveats: Specific trajectory networks and their hierarchy are proposed mechanisms supported indirectly by reviewed data; direct tests and developmental extensions remain open.
